page: Google Cloud Platform c4d-highcpu-96 is an x86_64 architecture server instance within the c4d family. It features 96 dedicated vCPUs and 180.0 GB of system memory. This configuration yields a memory-to-vCPU ratio of approximately 1.88 GB per core, positioning the instance as a compute-heavy resource.

The instance does not include local storage or integrated GPU hardware, meaning all storage requirements must be met via network-attached volumes. Additionally, it does not bundle complimentary public IPv4 addresses. These hardware constraints represent a tradeoff, prioritizing raw CPU allocation over local storage speed and graphics acceleration.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c4d-highcpu-96 offers high compute density relative to its memory footprint, making it a viable option for workloads that require substantial processing power without massive memory requirements. Suitable workloads include compute-bound tasks such as batch processing, high-performance computing simulations, and CPU-intensive compilation or encoding pipelines.
